newsitem.title: USA: Cyrix to unveil new Pentium clone chips.
newsitem.headline: Cyrix to unveil new Pentium clone chips.

text.p: Computer chip maker Cyrix Corp. said it will introduce on Friday its latest challenge to Intel Corp. with a microprocessor that will compete with the Pentium II at half the price.

Both Cyrix and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. are launching serious attempts this year in an effort to dethrone Intel, the world's biggest chip maker, after other efforts failed in the past due to product delays. AMD's K6 chip will begin shipping in some personal computers this summer.

"We think this is the year of the alternative processor," said Stan Swearington, a director of product marketing at Cyrix in Richardson, Texas. "Everyone who is talking to AMD is also talking to us. We offer a great value."
Swearington said the new chip, the 6x86MX, is currently being tested and evaluated by some major PC vendors.

The only major PC vendor AMD has signed up so far is Digital Equipment Corp., which is suing Intel for patent infringement on its Alpha chip designs. AMD's customers are mostly so-called second and third tier PC vendors in Asia.
AMD of Sunnyvale, Calif., has said other major PC vendors will be announced and Cyrix said it hoped to announce a "top tier" PC vendor in a few months.

Cyrix's new chip, formerly code-named the M2, will be in volume production in third quarter this year. Cyrix said the new processor delivers Penium II type performance and its lower prices will enable systems vendors sell powerful PCs for under $2,000. Cyrix said it expects to drive the prices for very high-performance multimedia PCs below $1,500.

Cyrix said its new processor will be priced at $190 for the 166 megahertz version, $240 for the 200 megahertz chip and $320 for its fastest 233 megahertz chip, in quantities of 1,000. A 266 megahertz model is expected in the fourth quarter. The lower speed chips will compete with Intel's Pentium MMX chips which provide better multimedia functions.
Editors at PC World, a popular computer magazine, said they evaluated prototypes of the Cyrix 6x86MX processor and that the Cyrix chip sets a new standard for price and performance.

"The 6x86MX chip...has the potential to shake up an already volatile PC market," said Charles Piller, executive news editor for PC World. Piller added that Cyrix's prices were well below AMD's prices.
Earlier this month, Intel launched its Pentium II processor at its fastest speeds to date.
Still, some analysts doubted Cyrix will make a dent in Intel's domination of the PC industry.
